method: Joint attack/defence likelihood with club parameters shared across E0/E1, separate scoring intercepts and home advantages per division, and a separate past-only goals-per-shot scale for each division. All other settings retain the fixed ELC shot recipe. Keep E1-only Elo as the unchanged 25% component to isolate the new attack/defence history.
informationFence: Both divisions exclude the target day and the immediately preceding calendar day; all shot scales, likelihood terms, team overlap and history diagnostics are computed only from earlier observations inside the same 1095-day window.
dataValidation: Validate E0 and E1 codes, complete closed-season counts (380 and 552), source SHA-256, shared canonical club names, unique fixtures and the rule that a club can occupy only one division per season. Missing shots fall back to verified goals without dropping a fixture. Preserve the original E1 data and target outcomes exactly.
identifiability: Relative club strengths across divisions are connected only by clubs with earlier matches in both divisions. Report those bridge clubs; do not infer a reliable division-strength gap from scoring averages or invent a manual promotion adjustment.
subgroup: Report, without selecting on it, matches where at least one club has fewer than 20 earlier E1 matches but at least 20 earlier E0 matches inside the training window.
pointGate: Both errors improve over the fixed E1-only shot model and v1 in every reported period
historicalGate: Point gate plus audit paired UTC-day bootstrap interval upper bounds below zero for both errors against both references
limitations: All ELC evaluation periods have been inspected in earlier experiments. This is retrospective development, not an untouched test or a new prospective score.
A shared club strength assumes useful persistence across seasons. Transfers, coaches and current roster changes are not modelled.
Same-division goals and home advantages remain separate. Cross-division strength is learned indirectly from clubs moving between divisions, not from direct inter-division league matches.
Clubs arriving from League One receive no additional lower-division history in this two-division experiment.
Shots on target are a proxy rather than measured xG. Dates lack reliable result-publication timestamps, so the previous calendar day is excluded conservatively.
The fixed E1-only Elo component remains unchanged; this experiment does not tune a new shared Elo or search for new mixture weights.
No historical result can authorize an automatic public-model change. The existing 100-match and 36-match packets remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
